voyage.name: Cathédrale Notre Dame
voyage.content: Built between 1176 and 1439 and with a 142-m tower (the highest cathedral tower in France), the Gothic cathedral is undoubtedly Strasbourg's finest architectural highlight. Check out the astrometric clock inside the cathedral.

voyage.name: Musée de l'Oeuvre Notre Dame - Medieval and Renaissance Art
voyage.content: A splendid museum of medieval religious art related to the cathedral.

voyage.name: Maison Kammerzell
voyage.content: The intricately carved half-timbered frames decorating the upper floors date from 1589.

voyage.name: Palais des Rohan
voyage.content: French-style palace, built after the acquisition of the town by the French (1681). Home to the Museum of Fine Arts, the Archaeological Museum and the Museum of Applied Arts.

voyage.name: Musée Alsacien
voyage.content: This museum features articles from the daily lives of Alsatian peoples from the 13th to 19th centuries: clothing, furniture, toys, tools of artisans and farmers, and religious objects used in Christian, Jewish, and even pagan rites. The exhibits are in rooms connected by wooden staircases and balconies in adjacent multistory Renaissance-era houses around a central courtyard.

voyage.name: Ponts Couverts
voyage.content: The Ponts Couverts are three bridges dominated by four towers from the 12th and 14th centuries. The bridges got their name from their roofs, which they lost in the 18th century. The towers are the remains of the ancient ramparts.

voyage.name: Barrage Vauban
voyage.content: The Barrage Vauban is a bridge, weir and defensive work erected in the 17th century. At that time, it was known as the Great Lock (grande écluse), although it does not function as a navigation lock in the modern sense of the word. Today it serves to display sculptures and has a viewing terrace on its roof, with views of the earlier Ponts Couverts bridges and Petite France quarter.

voyage.name: Council of Europe's seat
voyage.content: Built in 1977 by Henry Bernard.

voyage.name: European Court of Human Rights
voyage.content: Built in 1995 by Richard Rogers

voyage.name: European Parliament
voyage.content: The parliament tends to meet in Brussels more and the arrangement with the parliament moving shop between Brussels and Strasbourg several times a year has been criticized as wasteful of money by EU skeptics and penny-pinchers.

voyage.name: Parc de l'Orangerie
voyage.content: A beautiful classical park. It has a small free zoo featuring birds and a few other animals. Also has an excellent playground for young children.

voyage.name: Stockfeld
voyage.content: Garden city built in the early 20th century in the south-east of the Neuhof (southern part of the town). Use bus line #24 to get there.

voyage.name: B-line tramway terminus at Hoenheim
voyage.content: Built in 2001 by the contemporary architect Zaha Hadid.

voyage.name: Place de la République
voyage.content: A central crossroad encircled by neoclassical public buildings.

voyage.name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
voyage.content: It's recommended also because of the interesting building.

voyage.name: Historical Museum
voyage.content: Museum of Strasbourg's history.

voyage.name: Le Vaisseau
voyage.content: Science center for kids 3-15.

voyage.name: Lalique Museum
voyage.price: €8 adults; €4 children 6-18 and students; children under 6 are free
voyage.hours: Apr-Sep: daily 09:30-18:30; Feb Mar Oct Nov: Tue-Sat 10:00-18:00; Dec: daily 10:00-18:00; closed 25 Dec and January
voyage.content: A very large collection of works by René Lalique, a renowned French glassmaker and jeweller active from the 1880s until his death in 1945. The museum is adjacent to the sole production facility operated by Lalique (the company he founded), opened in 1921 and is on the site of a glass-making factory dating to the 18th century.

voyage.name: Place des Halles
voyage.content: A shopping centre with over 100 shops and restaurants north of the city center, but within walking distance.

voyage.name: Shopping centre Rivetoile
voyage.content: This new development has shops similar to Place des Halles as well as higher budget shops and a selection of cafes.

voyage.name: Au Brasseur
voyage.content: This a restaurant and microbrewery. Try one of their beers and a tarte flambé. Has a small children's menu.

voyage.name: Flam's
voyage.content: Serves a great variety of flams (tartes flambés) and has an amazing winelist for a budget joint.

voyage.name: L'Épicerie
voyage.content: Features sandwiches "tartines". Food from noon to night. Tables on street and inside.

voyage.name: Le Frangin
voyage.content: Two doors down from Flam's, it serves a wide range of home-cooked pasta and pizzas at reasonable prices. Offering pizza and pasta main courses, meat dishes and Alsatian beer. The owner is friendly and the food is good, satisfying Italian cooking.

voyage.name: Restaurant universitaire La Gallia
voyage.content: The oldest university restaurant in France, in a 19th-century building, built by the Germans (which explains the ceiling decorations). It is the last French university restaurant that is managed by students. Not a culinary triumph, but very affordable.

voyage.name: Le Saladin
voyage.content: Tunisian/Algerian couscous and kebabs. No alcohol.

voyage.name: Le Zorba
voyage.content: This little Greek restaurant in the Krutenau area features sandwiches, souvlaki, and kebabs.

voyage.name: Al Boustane
voyage.content: This Lebanese restaurant features sandwiches and kebabs.

voyage.name: Chez Yvonne
voyage.content: Usually frequented by Jacques Chirac, when he comes to Strasbourg, because of its well-known tête de veau (cooked veal head). More expensive.

voyage.name: Au Petit Bois Vert
voyage.content: In the Petite France district, serves well-prepared flams and Alsatian specialties in a small room with smiling waiters. The chef usually comes by at the end of the evening. Great terrace during the summer under a big tree on the bank of the river. No reservation, mid-range prices.

voyage.name: Maison Kirn
voyage.content: The restaurant is above a fine Alsatian specialty food shop on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Au Dauphin
voyage.content: Try the choucroute aux trois poissons; it is very fresh and a wonderful take on the traditional sauerkraut dish. They also serve the traditional choucroute garnie, with up to seven types of meat, including headcheese.

voyage.name: Restaurant Au Sanglier
voyage.content: A small restaurant with a traditional setting. If you want a Baeckoffe, you must inform the restaurant 24 hr before. Mid-range prices.

voyage.name: Les BerThoM
voyage.content: Beer bar near la place Gutenburg. Spacious with an agreeable atmosphere.

voyage.name: Café Bar de l'Odyssée
voyage.content: Bar with an intimate interior. Great place to enjoy a game of backgammon.

voyage.name: CIARUS
voyage.content: offers a variety of hostel accommodation, with rooms from 1 to 8 beds. Rates start at €27/night, and there's a canteen.

voyage.name: Auberge de Jeunesse HI Strasbourg
voyage.content: 20 minutes bus ride from town and fifteen minutes from the European Institutions, this youth hostel is in a leafy suburb close to the Rhine.

voyage.name: Auberge de Jeunesse René Cassin
voyage.content: Ten minutes from the city centre, this hostel offers a restaurant, bar and activities for guests.

voyage.name: Hôtel F1
voyage.content: A budget hotel.

voyage.name: PV-Holidays Adagio Strasbourg Place Kleber
voyage.content: Self-catering apartments situated in the heart of the historical quarter of the “Grande île”, just 10 minutes walk from the TGV station. Each of the 57 apartments sleep 2-4 people, are air-conditioned and completely fitted out: kitchen, television with international channels, etc. Located in the centre of the Alsatian capital makes this Aparthotel an ideal stopover location for business trips or for a long weekend. C

voyage.name: Hôtel Cathédrale
voyage.content: Best location of any hotel in Strasbourg, stylishly decorated, and more affordable for rooms without views of the cathedral.

voyage.name: Hotel Hannong
voyage.content: It has a stylish bar and restaurant, facing a fairly quiet street.

voyage.name: Hôtel Vendôme
voyage.address: 9, place de la Gare / 19 rue du Maire Kuss
voyage.content: 10 minutes from the Cathedral. Free wireless internet.

voyage.name: Mercure Strasbourg Centre Gare Hotel
voyage.content: A 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Château de Pourtalès
voyage.content: A 3-star hotel.

voyage.name: Régent Contades
voyage.content: An old building in the heart of the city.

voyage.name: Sofitel Strasbourg Grande Ile
voyage.content: Not far from both the Cathedral and Petite France.
